title: AI agent incident record
description: One publicly documented AI-agent or LLM-application security event, coded under the codebook in docs/codebook.md. The eight coded fields (type, lens, vector, channel_in, authority, channel_out, adversarial, outcome) keep the codes of the paper 'AI as Weapon, Target, and Surface' (2026) unchanged.

id.description: Zero-padded sequence number in the order of date and, within a month, of name. The paper cites event n as D-n. The file is named <id>-<slug>.json.

date.description: Month (YYYY-MM) or day (YYYY-MM-DD) in which the event was publicly reported or confirmed in the sources collected; not the month the attack began or was fixed.

name.description: Short descriptive title, in the vendor's or researcher's wording where one exists.

type.description: What kind of record the event is; decided by the genre of the primary source.

lens.description: The role AI plays in the event.

vector.description: How the attacker content or the failure got in; one value, the main mechanism in the primary source.

channel_in.description: The channel through which attacker content reached the AI component; for an event without an adversary, the channel of the input that triggered the behaviour.

authority.description: The capability that the compromised or misbehaving component, or the stolen or exposed credential, gave the event.

channel_out.description: How the effect left the system or took hold.

adversarial.description: Whether an attack technique is part of the event.

outcome.description: The most severe harm class that the primary source reports as realised or demonstrated.

cve.description: CVE identifiers assigned to the event; empty if none; the single token 'multiple' where the source reports several without listing them.

url.description: An https URL. The first entry is the primary source that was opened and read to code the event.

accessed.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) on which the URL was last confirmed reachable.

sources.description: Public sources. The first is the primary source.

summary.description: One or two sentences with the facts needed to check the coding; not coded and not used in any analysis.

owasp_agentic.description: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026 edition) identifiers.

owasp_llm.description: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025 edition) identifiers.

mitre_atlas.description: MITRE ATLAS technique or sub-technique identifiers.

mappings.description: Cross-references to external frameworks. Empty arrays mean no confident mapping, not that none applies.

affected.description: Organisations, products and software frameworks involved, as named in the primary source.

tags.description: Free-form lowercase kebab-case keywords for search.

status.description: confirmed: the primary source was opened and read and supports the coding. reported: the event is known only second-hand or its primary source is no longer reachable. disputed: a party named in the record contests the facts or the coding.
